Park and Recreation Commission
  MINUTES October 7, 2021

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on October 7, 2021 via
Zoom. Commissioner Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:32 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Lee Denmon, District 1
  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore, District 3
  Commissioner Christopher Beck, District 4
  Sabrina Barnes, Director - Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Thomas Uwal, Human Services Superintendent
  Gilbert Gonzalez, Graffiti Abatement Supervisor
  Anthony Harris, Recreation Supervisor
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
  Aisha Thompson, City Clerk
Absent
  Commissioner Henry Brown, Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso, District 2

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner McLemore made a motion to approve the minutes from September 2, 2021.
Commissioner Beck seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Denmon, Beck and McLemore
  Nays: None

Staff Report

Stephanie Maldonado presented a staff report recommending the Park and Recreation Commission
discuss and recommend the Park Improvements Priority List for approval by the Mayor and Council
Members. Director Barnes gave a recap on Measure A’s as well as the priority list. The purpose of
the list is to assist the city with future park planning and serve as a guide for potential development,
serve as a guide for funding by Measure A and other funding mechanisms such as the city’s general
fund or other grant opportunities in short it will guide local decisions. Projects related to health and
safety do have the highest priority. The approach to the recommended projects developed by looking
at health and safety, needs of modernization or upgrading, improved aesthetics or just a general
need.

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission
  MINUTES October 7, 2021

There is a total of 11 projects recommended by staff including renovating of restrooms, upgrading of
ball fields, fencing, seats and scoreboards, renovating the picnic areas including, replacing of
signage and fencing, installation of fitness stations, upgrading the irrigation system, resurfacing the
pool deck, and installing of camera systems at Edward Vincent, Jr. Park. Director Barnes shared the
results of the poll taken at the September meeting. Commissioner Denmon asked will both restrooms
at Darby Park be renovated. Director Barnes indicated both restrooms will be done eventually, but
we don’t want to have them both out of service at the same time. Commissioner Denmon commented
the restroom near the wading pool next to the baseball field needs renovating first. The other
restroom located out by the other field is ok. Director Barnes stated we can prioritize the restroom
near the wading pool as the first one to be renovated. It will be a total new construction, we will
demolish and build new at the site. We will bring in some temporary restrooms to sit there. The bid
that recently came back to us for Vincent Park’s restroom is $600,000 so that’s not 10 projects that
could be four solid projects. Sports Supervisor Anthony Harris assisted in obtaining some preliminary
quotes for ballfields starting at $700,000 to almost one (1) million dollars depending on how we
address gophers at that field. The gopher wire alone was approximately $300,000. Looking to get
the most done with the money that we have. Director Barnes noted the Mayor and Council Members
are very interested in making sure that our parks are elevated and have committed funding in this
year’s budget. The goal is to do more projects having both general and grant funds. Wherever
possible, we’ll be looking to defray the cost to our general fund and use those funds secondarily.
Commissioner Beck agreed with Commissioner Denmon regarding the restrooms at Darby Park and
stated the cost will continue to increase probably to five (5%) percent, every month due to supply
chain, there is a shortage of supplies coming in and he is not surprise at the cost at all. Director
Barnes informed the Commission that she is waiting for the timeline of the construction as we are
ready to award a bid for a restroom at Vincent Park. The question is do we want a construction site
in February when there could be a number of eyes visiting the park. The resurfacing of the
playground equipment can be done quickly and we have received the authorization to replace
playground equipment. Commissioner McLemore asked what the turnaround time on getting the
restrooms rebuilt is. Director Barnes stated the working days for the restrooms is 180 days.
Commissioner McLemore commented about six (6) months. Commissioner Beck asked is a bid with
a certain dollar amount locked in at its price and if so, how long is it locked in for. Director Barnes
stated yes and the goal is to get them locked and start working. Commissioner Denmon asked if the
order that the projects are in now are the order by cost and will they remain the same or will there be
changes. Director Barnes answered it’s not based on cost, it’s based on ranking. Commissioner
Denmon commented in his opinion before the renovation of the shade structure at Vincent Park, the
renovation of the Darby Park should be done first. Commissioner Beck agreed. Commissioner
McLemore stated the restrooms should be priority not only for aesthetics but for safety.

Commissioner Beck made a motion to accept the priority list with the change that the renovation of
Darby Park Restroom be moved to priority number two (2) and Commissioner McLemore seconded.
The motion was approved as follows:
  Ayes: Commissioners McLemore, Beck and Denmon
  2
   Park and Recreation Commission
  MINUTES October 7, 2021

  Nays: None

Verbal Reports

Gilbert Gonzalez gave a verbal report on behalf of Parks Administration regarding the following:
  • On September 18, 2021, the Parks Division assisted in a beautification project along Hillcrest
  Blvd. planting 250 flats of snapdragon flowers.
  • On September 25, 2021, in conjunction with the NFL and volunteers, the Parks Division
  assisted in planting 67 trees at Vincent Park. 23 chinese elms, 23 camphor, 21 oak trees
  and 40 flats of flowers were also planted.
  • Staff has been working on replacing broken playground equipment at Simiski Park and
  exercise equipment at both Ash and Center Parks.
  • The Graffiti Abatement staff has been busy this past month in all districts especially District
  3, especially on the Westside entrance into the City. This area has been getting tagged very
  heavily.
  • District 4 has experienced heavy tagging as well off Prairie Avenue between Century Blvd.
  and Imperial Highway. Residents near Yukon have also been effected with heavy graffiti.
  • Graffiti staff also participated in the beautification project held at Vincent Park.

Commissioner McLemore stated at 317 La Brea there is graffiti on the side of the building. Gilbert
Gonzalez commented yes, the white vacant building. Commissioner McLemore confirmed. Mr.
Gonzalez stated he has reached out to Code Enforcement and has been informed they are in touch
with the owner of the building and currently in discussion as to whom will take care of the graffiti
currently on the roof. Mr. Gonzalez stated he’ll follow up with Code Enforcement and keep the
Commission updated. Commissioner Beck asked is the level of graffiti equal to what it normally is or
higher or lower. Mr. Gonzalez answered the graffiti level is higher than normal. Commissioner
Denmon stated there is a little walkway at Darby Park between the tennis courts and the baseball
field that’s not gated and noticed a substantial amount of graffiti on the ground there and wants to
know if that area has been reported. Mr. Gonzalez answered no, no one has reported that issue but
will have it resolved tomorrow.

Anthony Harris gave a verbal report on behalf of the Recreation Division regarding the following:
  • Early Learners Play to Learners Play to Learn Program: The department’s Early Learners
  Play to Learn Program returned to in-person instruction on Tuesday, September 21. The
  program provides an excellent school readiness experience for boys and girls ages 3 to 4.
  The program is designed to provide children with a diverse, exciting, and stimulating
  environment. Each class promotes learning through “hands-on” experiences. Projects and
  activities address a wide variety of school readiness, social and motor skills. All students
  must be potty-trained. Classes are held Tuesday through Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 12 p.m.
  Siminski Park and Lock haven Community Center focus on meeting the needs of children
  through this active time of growth. Students learn letter, shape and sound recognition, as
  well as the alphabets, numbers and simple words. The class is designed to prepare students

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission
  MINUTES October 7, 2021

  for kindergarten. Rogers Park offers a Spanish Immersion class for families who want to
  give their child the gift of bilingualism. The curriculum is designed for basic fluency and
  conversation. Students learn letters, shapes, numbers and simple words. All in Spanish!
  We are currently accepting enrollment. Interested persons should contact the Park,
  Recreation and Community Services Department.
  •  Youth Flag Football: Due to the most recent COVID-19 protocols for “Youth Sports”, we are
  not able to run our competitive flag football league as planned. However, we are beginning
  the Inglewood Rams Flag Football “Skills Clinics” this Saturday. We are pleased to offer 10
  consecutive weeks for 215 participants between the ages of 5 and 12. The specific goals
  and projected learning outcomes of the flag football clinics are as follows: get our youth out
  of the house, motivated and moving for weekly fitness for the body and developing “Football
  IQ” for the mind; introduction and execution of the necessary fundamentals involved with the
  game of flag football; having fun while competing in football specific skills, drills, and game
  like situations. Specific attention will be dedicated to the following: fundamental techniques
  of throwing, running, blocking, flag pulling, etc.; agility drills and overall body conditioning;
  methods involving player alignment and assignment and offensive and defensive concepts.
  Overall development and understanding of the sport of football; various competitions
  involving the skills, drills, techniques and concepts above. The fun begins this weekend and
  runs through December 11th. We will have Thursday Night Football clinics on November 4th
  and Monday Night Football clinics on November 22nd. We look forward to creating a sports
  environment founded on learning fundamentals, skill progression, competition, and FUN.
  •  Halloween Drive-Thru Experience: The Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Department is keeping the fun traditions and excitement of Halloween alive! Join us for a
  safe, family friendly Drive-Thru Halloween experience. There is no age limitation, however
  a few places can be a little spooky. The event will take place on Friday, October 29 and
  Saturday, October 30 from 6:00 to 10:00 p.m. at Grevillea Art Park (located across the street
  from Inglewood High School).This event is free; however, you must RSVP to receive an
  admission ticket for a selected day and time. This is a drive-thru event only. Windows down,
  masks on! Absolutely NO walk-ups allowed. All reservations must be made in advance.
  The registration link will open on Wednesday, October 13, 2021. RSVP for the event at
  www.cityofinglewood.org/2021Halloween.

Commissioner Beck asked if participants of the Halloween Drive-Thru Experience are permitted to
dress in their costumes with a mask. Mr. Harris answered absolutely.

Thomas Uwal gave a verbal report on behalf of the Human Services Division regarding the following:
  • CACFP: The Child Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) started on Monday, October 4, 2021.
  The program distributes meals to youth 18 and under at the following locations: Darby Park,
  Rogers Park and the Crenshaw Library operating five (5) days a week, Monday through
  Friday from 2:30 p.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Transportation: Our Senior and Disabled Transportation Program continues to effectively
  provide transportation to dialysis, doctor’s appointments, recreational places and the senior

  4
   Park and Recreation Commission
  MINUTES October 7, 2021

  center. All programs continue to require face mask and practicing social distancing. Still
  adhering to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) restricting participants to
  a limit of 10.
  •  Nutrition: Our Elderly Nutrition program continues meal delivery serving 300 seniors per
  week, while also distributing LA Food Bank and fresh produce weekly.
  •  Senior Center Classes, Programs and Activities: The Senior Center is providing limited
  classes and activities which consist of Tai Chi, chair exercise, Yoga, knitting and crochet.
  The Billiard Room, Computer Room and Gym have opened with limited participants not to
  exceed 15, maintaining social distancing and adhering to mask requirements. Although
  operating within limited capacity, staff is excited to see the seniors and the seniors who are
  able to visit exuberant the same energy.

Commissioner McLemore asked if the seniors are allowed to eat their lunch in the center. Mr. Uwal
answered no, the Senior Center is still closed and meals are being delivered but discussion has been
held on a future Grab n Go Service. Director Barnes added that she’d like to note that restrictions by
the Los Angeles County Health Department have been lifted, our funder Workforce Development
Aging and Community Services (WDACS) has implemented the restriction of operation to home
deliveries. Commissioner Denmon asked has the Los Angeles County Health Department
restrictions been lifted on all buildings in the city from being completely closed. Director Barnes stated
there are very few Public Safety Protocols still in place including sports programs and school
systems. Entertainment venues have lighten restrictions, major events have their mandatory safety
protocols. Our Parks and Recreation Centers are open with exceptions to our Early Learners
Program who follow a school like model and adhere to the city’s continuous safety protocols. Los
Angeles County’s numbers maybe low but the City of Inglewood’s remain high. The city remains
cautious. The Mayor and City Council do not meet with residents in their meeting space, and the
Commission isn’t either. Regarding the Recreation Centers, the population that is typically in the gym
playing basketball were among the highest in city numbers warranting the current restriction.
Activities are resuming inside the buildings on a case by case basis, keeping in mind what type of
risk or exposure it maybe. Commissioner Denmon asked when meetings are held, they are social
distanced and safety protocols are still in place. Director Barnes stated yes which includes the indoor
mask requirements, protocols of indoor meetings and the number of attendees allowed in a room.
Commissioner Beck stated that the seniors are the back bone of the city, being of the largest senior
populations in Los Angeles County. He asked if the seniors are receiving the same amount of meals
as they were during the height of the pandemic. Thomas Uwal stated during the pandemic the
number of meals did increase but now we are back to the regular meal schedule delivering 300 meals
per week with a total of approximately 1,500 meals a month. Commissioner Beck commented that’s
fantastic. Director Barnes stated last year there was a huge influx of money given to service our
seniors going from providing one (1) meal a day to an increase of two (2) and sometimes three (3)
meals per day for five (5) days. Our annual allocated budget is slightly over $14 million as opposed
to last year’s $12 million dollars that was received under the stay home order.

  5
   Park and Recreation Commission
  MINUTES October 7, 2021

Director’s Business

Director Barnes provided an update on monies received for the Capital Improvements Projects.
Measure A funds were approved for parks restrooms. The Mayor and Council also allocated funds
for the renovation of restrooms, picnic arbors, as well as the ballfields at Vincent Park. Those monies
will help with the total amounts using grant money first then using the general funds. Director Barnes
thanked all who attended, participated, contributed, or gave words of encouragement for the NFL
Green event. Director Barnes expressed the magnitude of number of trees and the man power it
entailed planting them, being the first of many and setting the bar. The NFL Green Program started
with us and will end with us. The final project will be on January 29, 2022 and will be the beautificatiion
of Queen Park - refreshing of the KaBOOM garden area. Both projects were jointly paid for by the
NFL and the city. There are many upcoming projects to look forward to in January with the NFL and
other agencies such as the American Heart Association, Play 60 and two (2) additional projects that
are in discussion prompting a lot of activity at Vincent Park, surrounding and leading up to the Super
Bowl.

Commissioners Comments

Commissioner Beck commented that he engaged recently with maintenance staff and just wanted
to share his interaction. He thanked staff and staff in return smiled and thanked him without knowing
who he was. Commissioner Beck encourages his Commissioners to share their appreciation to
others.

Commissioner Denmon commented that the Golden Shovel Event was a very nice event with the
NFL. He commended the workers for their contribution in assisting with the tree planting.

Public Comments

  None

Announcements

City of Inglewood’s Annual Turkey Giveaway will take place on November 23, 2021 at Hollywood
Park from 9:00 a.m. to noon. It will be a drive-thru event. Registration will be begin November 1,
2021.

The City’s Tree Lighting Ceremony will return to the Inglewood Forum on November 29, 2021 at 6:30
p.m.

With no further comments, the meeting was adjourned at 7:32 p.m.
